results.name: Chair Feet Elevated Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with both heels placed on the edge of a chair, legs bent at a 90-degree angle.
Position your arms by your sides with your palms facing down for stability.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your hips off the floor.
Hold the position briefly at the top, squeezing your glutes, then slowly lower your hips back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your heels remain firmly on the chair to provide a stable base for the movement.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement to enhance muscle engagement.
results.description: Chair Feet Elevated Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Lower Back.

results.name: Chair Frog Feet Elevated Glute Bridge Bodyweight
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels placed on the edge of a chair, legs bent, and the soles of your feet touching each other in a frog position.
Position your arms by your sides with your palms facing down for stability.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Hold the position briefly at the top, squeezing your glutes, then slowly lower your hips back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your heels remain firmly on the chair to provide a stable base for the movement.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your hips and inhaling as you lower them.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement to enhance muscle engagement.
Maintain the frog position with your feet to target the inner thighs and glutes more effectively.
results.description: Chair Frog Feet Elevated Glute Bridge Bodyweight is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs stacked, knees bent at about 90 degrees, and your hips aligned. Rest your head on your bottom arm and place your top hand on your hip for support.
Keep your feet together and your core engaged.
Raise your top knee upward as far as possible without rotating your hips or lifting your feet off each other. Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower your knee back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips stacked and avoid rolling your body backward as you lift your knee.
Engage your core throughout to stabilize your torso.
Use slow, controlled movements to maintain constant tension on the muscles.
results.description: Clamshell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hips.

results.name: Clap Curtsy Squat
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight overhead, palms facing each other.
Step your right foot behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy squat while simultaneously lower your hands in circular motion to your sides.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, extending your right leg back to shoulder-width apart and bringing your arms back overhead and clap them together.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on keeping your chest lifted and your back straight to avoid leaning forward.
Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially when lowering into the curtsy squat, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your front foot and does not extend past your toes.
results.description: Clap Curtsy Squat is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

results.name: Cossack Squat
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward.
Shift your weight to your right leg, bending your right knee while keeping your left leg straight. Lower your hips towards the floor, ensuring your right knee tracks over your right toes.

Push through your right heel to return to the starting position, then repeat the movement on the left side by shifting your weight to your left leg and bending your left knee. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on maintaining an upright chest and straight back to ensure proper form and prevent injury.
Perform the movement with control, especially when shifting your weight and lowering your hips, to maximize muscle activation.
Ensure your knee tracks over your toes during the squat to avoid unnecessary strain on your joints.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you descend and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Cossack Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Calves.

results.name: Counterbalanced Skater Squat
instructions: Stand tall on your right foot, curl your left leg to 90 degrees, and extend your arms forward.
Lower your hips while bending your right knee, lean forward, and maintain balance by moving your left thigh backward.
Hold this position for a while, return to the initial position, and repeat.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and balance.
Focus on maintaining an upright chest and straight back to ensure proper form and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lower into the squat and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure your knee tracks over your toes during the squat to avoid unnecessary strain on your joints.
results.description: Counterbalanced Skater Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Calves.

results.name: Crossed Arms Front Leg Kick
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms crossed in front of your chest.
Engage your core and lift your right leg straight in front of you to perform a front kick, keeping your leg as straight as possible.
Lower your right leg back to the starting position.
Immediately lift your left leg to perform a front kick, keeping your arms crossed and your core engaged. Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on maintaining an upright posture, avoiding leaning back or forward as you kick.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you kick and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure your kicks are performed with a controlled motion, avoiding any jerky movements.
results.description: Crossed Arms Front Leg Kick is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals.

results.name: Curtsy Lunge Bodyweight
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips or by your sides.
Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy lunge. Your front knee should be aligned with your front ankle.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side, stepping your left leg behind and across your right leg. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your torso upright throughout the exercise to maintain balance and proper form.
Ensure your front knee does not extend beyond your toes to protect your knees from strain.
Focus on pushing through your heel as you return to the starting position to engage your glutes.
results.description: Curtsy Lunge Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

results.name: Curtsy Lunge Slide With Towel
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and place a towel under your right foot.
Slide your right foot behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy lunge. Your front knee should be aligned with your front ankle.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, sliding your right foot back to the original position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one side, then switch the towel to the other foot and repeat the movement with the opposite leg.
tips: Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your front knee does not extend beyond your toes to protect your knees from strain.
Focus on pushing through your heel as you return to the starting position to engage your glutes.
Use a smooth surface to ensure the towel slides easily and reduces friction.
results.description: Curtsy Lunge Slide With Towel is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

results.name: Curtsy Lunges Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a resistance band under your left foot. Hold the handles of the band with both hands either at shoulder height or by your abdomen sides.
Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, while bending both knees to lower into a lunge.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, bringing your right leg back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to work the other leg.
tips: Keep your chest up and your back straight to maintain proper form.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you push back to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
results.description: Curtsy Lunges Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings.
